trigger: two threads on the shared FULLMUTEX connection; the step->changes pair is not atomic
policy_floor: explicit MUST in a .claude/routed-concerns.md row (sqlite3_changes idiom, #1033)
summary: sqlite3_changes() read after step() on a shared FULLMUTEX connection; FULLMUTEX serialises calls, not the pair. Wrong answer makes the collision check miss a real collision or refuse a valid batch. Converted to RETURNING. Found by walking the routed-concern table at Step 0, before any agent ran.
classification_rationale: the code used an idiom a routed-concern row explicitly forbids for new/modified stores

trigger: mutating the ROLLBACK on the event-insert failure path to COMMIT
policy_floor: a FALSE-GREEN test offered as closure evidence
summary: Atomicity test named 'rolls back the cursor when the event insert fails' dropped the table, so the first statement failed and nothing ever inserted; it passed with no transaction at all. Replaced with a mid-batch refusal asserting the already-inserted row is gone; mutation-verified to kill the COMMIT-for-ROLLBACK mutant.
classification_rationale: the test's name asserted a behaviour its assertions could not observe

trigger: a source violates rule 3(a) or two OS records derive one record_key
summary: The atomic inserts returned bool, collapsing a transient failure (retry succeeds) with a key collision (retrying re-refuses forever). The contract's own retain-and-retry rule then guaranteed an infinite loop: cursor frozen, queue never draining, capture dead, one repeating log line the only symptom. Now std::expected<void, CursorInsertError> with a KeyCollision discriminant. E6 today only because no collector ships; HIGH once one lands, and these are frozen signatures.
classification_rationale: the return type could not express a distinction the contract depends on

trigger: a persisted record_key or payload field carrying an embedded NUL (fixed-width USB descriptor, EvtRender buffer)
summary: sqlite3_bind_text with length -1 truncates at the first NUL, while the enclosing helper already bound source/cursor_json with an explicit size. A record_key of '\0a' is non-empty in C++ but binds as zero-length, collapsing distinct keys onto one row; a truncated payload field then mismatches on replay and wedges the source. The readback had the same trap via string_view-from-char*. Both sides now carry explicit lengths and a NUL-bearing key is refused.
classification_rationale: the bind length contradicted the guard the same function relies on

trigger: a transient SQLite failure while reading <name>_lookback_seconds
summary: get_config returns the caller's default for both 'unset' and 'unreadable', so an operator's lookback of 0 (the works-council forward-only lever cited in the manual and the SOC 2 inventory) silently became a 7-day retrospective read on a transient failure: a privacy control failing OPEN. Added try_get_config (tri-state, same shape as get_cursor) and lookback_seconds_or_forward_only, and rule 5 now states an unreadable lookback is 0. HIGH once a collector consumes it.
classification_rationale: the control's documented behaviour was not what the read path produced

trigger: a consumer author reading the frozen header's banner
summary: Banner rule 6 still described snapshot()/ack(n), the positional API this change DELETED, in the header the routed-concern row calls the full contract. It would have instructed both consumers to reimplement the exact overflow race the change exists to close.
classification_rationale: the contract text named an API the class does not expose

trigger: a consumer's start() throws (permission denied on an event-log channel, netlink bind failure)
summary: A source whose start() threw was logged 'continuing without it' but stayed in cursor_sources_, so collect() drove it every tick against an unarmed subscription and it returned ordinary Advanced/0-event results forever: a dead source reporting health. It also never received the on_enabled_changed(false) the same block argues must precede the first callback. Now dropped.
classification_rationale: the log line asserted a removal the code did not perform

trigger: any reader of the manual, the GUI configure surface or the SOC 2 inventory
summary: 'The FIRST default-on capture source' was asserted on seven surfaces and is false: process, tcp, service, user and perf are already default-on, and the branch's own registry test asserts it. In the SOC 2 inventory this would make a works-council scoping exercise under-count five already-collecting sources, one of which the same inventory classifies as behavioural telemetry containing PII. Corrected to 'first works-council-class source' everywhere. content/definitions/tar.yaml separately told the operator power is 'not usage-class data' while the SOC 2 doc classifies it as usage-class and co-determination-relevant; the yaml now agrees.
classification_rationale: the claim contradicted the registry and the branch's own test

trigger: a wave-2 author copying the only CursorSource in the tree
summary: The fake CursorSource returned an outcome on a failed persist, which rule 3 forbids and names as the exact shape to avoid ('reports a clean tick while nothing was written'). It is the only implementation in the tree and its own header claimed it persists 'exactly as a real wave-2 source must'. It now throws IncompleteCaptureError.
classification_rationale: the fixture contradicted the contract it advertised as demonstrating

trigger: an operator reading the OS compatibility matrix the manual's own intro points them at
summary: The OS compatibility matrix and warehouse tables gained no rows for either new source, though every other queryable-empty source has one and the modified intro sentence directs readers there. Rows added for both.
classification_rationale: a required user-manual section for a changed operator surface (item 2)
